title: The Bright Sun Brings it to Light

keywords: the bright sun brings it to light
full_text:
A wandering tailor's apprentice had spent his last farthing and was trudging down a deserted highway when he met an honest old Jew carrying a heavy pack of goods. Driven by desperate greed, the youth struck the traveler down, demanding his money.

As the old man lay dying upon the dusty road, he pointed with a trembling finger toward the morning sun rising over the hills, whispering his final words: "The bright sun will bring it to light!"

The apprentice scoffed, took the meager bag of copper coins, and fled. Years passed, and the crime remained buried. The tailor married, prospered, and became a respected master in a flourishing town, surrounded by loving children and honored by his neighbors.

One bright morning, as he sat at the breakfast table drinking hot coffee, the morning sun shone brightly through the windowpane, casting shimmering reflections across the foam in his cup. The master smiled absentmindedly and muttered aloud, "It would bring it to light, indeed! How absurd!"

His wife asked what he meant by such curious words. Feeling completely secure after so many years, the man foolishly confessed the murder he had committed in his youth, laughing at the dying man's warning.

Horrified by the dark truth, the wife reported the confession to the magistrates. The master was arrested, confessed before the court, and paid the penalty for his ancient crime, proving that though justice may tarry, the bright sun of truth inevitably illuminates every shadow.
moral: No crime remains hidden forever; the light of truth exposes the darkest deeds.
